ec-l3-full.title: Lesson 3 Master Quiz: Properties of a Well-Written Text & Modes of Expression
ec-l3-full.desc: Test your mastery over all 44 slide concepts including Unity, Coherence, Cohesion, 5 Organizational Patterns, Language Appropriateness, Personal Narratives, Journaling, and Multimodal Expression.

questions.q: What two essential qualities must a text have to achieve its goals of informing, inspiring, or entertaining?
questions.exp: As stated in the slides, writing is intended to inform, inspire, or entertain readers, but to achieve these goals, a text needs to have UNITY and CONNECTEDNESS.

questions.q: Which property refers to how well the parts of a text fit together so that all sentences develop the main idea and each paragraph deals with a single main idea?
questions.exp: Unity refers to how well the parts of a text fit together to form a whole, where all sentences develop the main idea and each paragraph covers one main idea.

questions.q: What is the distinction between 'Organization' and 'Order' according to the lesson?
options: Organization is about grammar, while Order is about vocabulary.
Organization is the logical arrangement of ideas to make the message easier to understand, while Order refers to your choice of what to mention first, second, next, etc.
Organization is for spoken speech, while Order is only for written essays.
They are identical synonyms with no distinction.
questions.exp: Organization is the logical arrangement of ideas to make comprehension easier; Order refers to your sequential choice of what to mention first, second, next, and so on.

questions.q: Which organizational pattern proceeds from specific details to general ideas, summarizing everything into a main idea at the end?
questions.exp: Inductive organization moves from specific details to general conclusions (represented by a triangle pointing up: Specific at apex, Broad at base).

questions.q: Which organizational pattern is represented by an inverted triangle (Broad at top base to Specific at bottom apex)?
questions.exp: Deductive organization starts with a broad general idea/thesis and proceeds downward into specific supporting details and examples.

questions.q: A paragraph describing the Bahay ni Rizal by first encountering the museum pavilion, then the reconstructed nipa-and-bamboo house, and then the adjacent plaza area uses which pattern?
questions.exp: Spatial order organizes details according to physical location and sensory perspective to help readers visualize a layout.

questions.q: An excerpt tracing Bahay ni Rizal from Rizal's birth in 1861, through the Spanish and American periods, to 20th-century restoration and its modern status uses which pattern?
questions.exp: Chronological order organizes events along a historical or temporal timeline.

questions.q: Which property refers to the overall oneness of ideas, sentences, and paragraphs where all relevant ideas stick together?
questions.exp: Coherence refers to the overall oneness of ideas, sentences, and paragraphs where all relevant ideas stick together.

options: Electronic devices used for giving PowerPoint presentations
Words and phrases that act as bridges between ideas to develop, relate, and move them
Punctuation marks used exclusively at the end of paragraphs
Digital algorithms for converting audio into text
questions.exp: Transitional devices are words and phrases that act as bridges between ideas to develop, relate, and move them.

questions.q: Why is a Personal Narrative classified as an example of 'Subjective Narration'?
options: Because it is written exclusively in the third-person objective point of view.
Because it presents a story based mainly on personal feelings, impressions, and lived perspective ('I', 'me', 'we').
Because it contains only legal facts and statistics.
Because it must be verified by an external editorial board.
questions.exp: Personal narratives recount events from the author's subjective viewpoint using sensory details and personal emotions.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the 6 essential components of a Journal Entry?
questions.exp: The 6 components are: Today's Date, Notable Experiences, Mood or Emotion, Thoughts and Reflections, Goals and Plans, and Drawings or Photos.

questions.q: What ethical guiding principle is highlighted for digital posts and Multimodal Expression?
questions.exp: The lesson reminds students that every digital post leaves an imprint, so one must 'think before you click' to ensure ethical and responsible expression.

ec-l4-full.title: Lesson 4 Master Quiz: Reflective Communication & Metacognition
ec-l4-full.desc: Evaluate your understanding of the 4 Core Processes of Communication, Metacognition, Lucas (2020) Framework, Reflective Expression Pillars, and the 4 Growth Strategies.

questions.q: What are the four core processes in the human communication loop?
questions.exp: The four core processes in Lesson 4 are Interpreting, Engaging, Expressing, and Reflecting.

questions.q: How is 'Metacognition' fundamentally defined in communication psychology?
options: Communicating through digital avatars in the metaverse
Thinking about thinking — the conscious monitoring and regulation of one's own thought and communicative processes
questions.exp: Metacognition is defined as 'thinking about thinking'—the conscious awareness and self-regulation of one's cognitive and communicative strategies.

questions.q: According to Lucas (2020), what role does reflection play in interpersonal dialogue?
options: It delays speech unnecessarily during rapid negotiations.
It transforms raw communication experiences into actionable self-knowledge and ethical relational growth.
It is only necessary when giving formal political speeches.
It eliminates the need for receiving audience feedback.
questions.exp: Lucas (2020) underscores reflection as an essential competency for transforming communication into deeper ethical and personal insight.

questions.q: Which pillar of Reflective Expression involves authentic emotional honesty and expressing needs without defensiveness?
questions.exp: Vulnerability is the pillar characterized by emotional authenticity, openness, and courageous expression.

questions.q: What are the four Actionable Growth Strategies for developing reflective communication competence?
options: Setting Clear Goals, Seeking Feedback, Intentional Practice, Tracking Progress
Talking Faster, Using Jargon, Avoiding Public Speaking, Reading Silently
Memorizing Vocabulary, Taking Speed Tests, Ignoring Criticism, Multitasking
Recording Videos, Posting Daily, Buying Equipment, Gaining Followers
questions.exp: The four actionable growth strategies are: Setting Clear Goals, Seeking Feedback, Intentional Practice, and Tracking Progress.
